title: A newer passed run with only unclassified stages (e.g. cargo fmt --check) refuses evaluation over an earlier eligible acknowledged test run on the same commit
outcome: A newer passed run with only unclassified stages (e.g. cargo fmt --check) refuses evaluation over an earlier eligible acknowledged test run on the same commit
acceptance: When the newest terminal committed-input run of a claim at the judged commit passed, but has only stages TermAl cannot record as test or build (so it can never produce a verification record), committed-input admission skips it. Admission is then decided by the next older applicable run at the same commit, exactly as if the skipped run did not exist. A behavioural test registers a passed, acknowledged cargo test run and then a passed fmt-only run on the same clean commit, and shows the evaluation is admitted on the test run.

A newer run that failed, or whose state is unknown, keeps today's refusal; a coherent unfinished newer run and a run on another commit keep today's handling (skipped, and never themselves able to admit). The newest-terminal-result rule settled in w-e66983e3d919 is otherwise unchanged. Behavioural tests show that a failed fmt-only run and an unknown-state fmt-only run both still refuse, and that an unfinished or other-commit run cannot by itself supply admission.
A run with only unclassified stages that is the only candidate still refuses with verification_record_unclassified_stages and its remedy text.
